AI.motivation: Existing research on educational chatbots relies on small samples and self-reported data, lacking large-scale evidence on actual usage behavior.
AI.method: Descriptive analysis of objective log data from 77,543 distance-learning students, examining usage patterns across demographic and structural variables (gender, age group, study cluster, degree, study mode).
AI.result: Syntea is embedded in study routines of many learners, but usage differs across demographic and structural contexts.
AI.conclusion: The findings provide an empirical basis for further development of AI-based learning support and contribute a large-scale analysis of educational chatbot usage in higher education.

title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation
summary: Scientific ideas rarely start from a blank page. They inherit mechanisms, repair known limitations, and recombine pieces of earlier work, much like biological genomes. Current benchmarks still say little about whether AI systems can follow this inheritance structure. We present IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a benchmark for scientific lineage reasoning and lineage-grounded idea generation. IG-Bench is organized around the IdeaGene framework: each paper or proposal is represented as a set of minimal, typed, evidence-grounded Idea Genome objects, and a GenomeDiff aligns these objects to record inheritance, mutation, loss, external import, and novel insertion under six operational evolutionary dynamics. The benchmark contains 1,961 golden lineage traces, 1,085 curated Idea Genome objects, and 920 pairwise GenomeDiff records across 10 scientific domains. It supports two evaluations. IG-Exam (42 task types, 1,029 instances) tests closed-form lineage reasoning across Idea Genome abstraction, inheritance tracing, evolutionary reasoning, and lineage verification. IG-Arena evaluates generation with a lineage-conditioned Population-Evolution Score(PES), asking whether a proposal can be inserted as a coherent descendant of a given lineage population: it should inherit the right Idea Genome objects, vary meaningfully from nearby work, and offer selection value for future research. Experiments on 14 LLM-based scientists expose a compositional bottleneck. The strongest system reaches only 27.3% exact accuracy on lineage reasoning, and structured lineage context reshuffles system rankings rather than helping every participant uniformly.

AI.tldr: IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench) evaluates AI systems on scientific lineage reasoning and lineage-grounded idea generation across 10 domains, revealing that current LLM-based scientists achieve only 27.3% exact accuracy on reasoning and that structured lineage context reshuffles rankings rather than uniformly helping.
AI.motivation: Current benchmarks fail to assess whether AI systems can follow the inheritance structure of scientific ideas (inheriting mechanisms, repairing limitations, recombining prior work), motivating a benchmark grounded in evolutionary dynamics of scientific progress.
AI.method: IG-Bench uses the IdeaGene framework: papers/proposals are represented as typed, evidence-grounded Idea Genome objects, with GenomeDiff recording inheritance, mutation, loss, external import, and novel insertion under six evolutionary dynamics. It contains 1,961 lineage traces, 1,085 Idea Genome objects, and 920 pairwise GenomeDiff records. It provides IG-Exam (42 task types, 1,029 instances) for closed-form reasoning and IG-Arena for generation evaluated via Population-Evolution Score (PES).
AI.result: The strongest LLM-based scientist achieved only 27.3% exact accuracy on lineage reasoning; structured lineage context reshuffled system rankings instead of uniformly improving performance, exposing a compositional bottleneck.
AI.conclusion: Current AI systems struggle with the compositional and evolutionary structure of scientific idea generation, and IG-Bench reveals fundamental limitations in reasoning about scientific lineage and generating coherent descendants.
